name: Madrid
summary: Spain's capital of museums, plazas and late dinners, and the easiest base for day trips to Toledo and Segovia by high-speed train.

tips.title: 90 days in any 180
tips.body: Visa-free visitors can stay in the Schengen area, which includes Spain, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Earlier Schengen visits in those 180 days count, and overstaying can bring a ban of up to 3 years.

tips.title: Check your passport dates
tips.body: Your passport must be issued less than 10 years before you arrive and expire at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area.

tips.title: Fingerprints at the border (EES)
tips.body: The EU Entry/Exit System replaces passport stamps. On your first visit you may register fingerprints and a photo at a booth before passport control. It's free, and the record lasts 3 years.

tips.title: ETIAS isn't running yet
tips.body: ETIAS, the EU's online travel authorisation for visa-free visitors, was not yet operational in August 2026 and was expected to launch in late 2026. It is not a visa. Check before you fly.

tips.title: Have proof ready at the border
tips.body: Border officers may ask to see a return or onward ticket, travel insurance, enough money for your stay and where you are staying.

tips.title: Watch for pickpockets
tips.body: Be alert to street crime. Thieves use distraction techniques and often work in teams. Don't leave your passport at hotel reception to collect later.

tips.title: Carry photo ID
tips.body: You must show photo ID if a police officer asks.

tips.title: Keep your drink in sight
tips.body: Buy your own drinks and keep them in sight so they can't be spiked.

tips.title: Emergency number 112
tips.body: Call 112 for police, ambulance or fire.

tips.title: Get travel insurance
tips.body: UK and EU visitors can use a GHIC or EHIC for state healthcare, but it is not a replacement for travel insurance.

tips.title: Summer heat and wildfires
tips.body: Extreme heat hits much of Spain in summer. Starting a wildfire is a crime even by accident, so take care with cigarettes and barbecues.

tips.title: Declare €10,000 or more in cash
tips.body: Cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when you enter or leave the EU. Use official exchange offices or banks to change money.

tips.title: No meat or dairy in your bag
tips.body: You can't bring meat, milk or products containing them into the EU from outside it, with a few exceptions.

tips.title: Check trains after the Toledo crash
tips.body: Gov.uk reported a high-speed rail collision in Toledo on 28 October 2026. Check Renfe for disruption to Madrid–Toledo trains before a day trip; Renfe's helpline is +34 900 10 10 20.

places.name: Madrid Atocha station
places.blurb: Main station for high-speed trains to Toledo.

places.name: Toledo Cathedral
places.blurb: Gothic Primate Cathedral of Spain, the centrepiece of the walled old city.
places.tip: Monday to Saturday 10 am to 6:30 pm, Sunday 2 pm to 6:30 pm; last entry 30 minutes before.

places.name: Synagogue of El Tránsito
places.tip: Tuesday to Saturday 9:30 am to 8 pm, Sundays and holidays 10 am to 3 pm, closed Mondays.

places.name: Mosque of Cristo de la Luz
places.blurb: Small mosque from the year 999, later a church, one of Toledo's 'three cultures' sights.

places.name: Madrid Chamartín station
places.blurb: Station for high-speed trains to Segovia.

places.name: Roman Aqueduct of Segovia
places.blurb: Roman aqueduct with 166 arches striding through the city centre.

places.name: Alcázar of Segovia
places.blurb: Fairytale castle on a rock above two rivers, said to have inspired Disney's Cinderella castle.
places.tip: 10 am to 6 pm (Nov to Mar), 10 am to 7:30 pm (Apr to Oct).

places.name: Segovia Cathedral
places.blurb: Late-Gothic cathedral on the Plaza Mayor.

places.name: Mesón de Cándido
places.blurb: Famous restaurant at the foot of the aqueduct, known for cochinillo asado (roast suckling pig).

itineraries.title: Toledo day trip from Madrid
itineraries.creator: willflyforfood
itineraries.summary: The 'City of the Three Cultures', about half an hour from Madrid by high-speed train: the cathedral, El Tránsito synagogue and the Cristo de la Luz mosque.

items.name: AVE from Atocha to Toledo
items.note: About 35 minutes, then a 10 to 15 minute walk up to the old city. Gov.uk reported a high-speed rail collision near Toledo on 28 Oct 2026: check Renfe before you go.

items.name: Toledo Cathedral
items.note: The guide suggests a guided tour to get the most out of Toledo.

items.name: Mosque of Cristo de la Luz

itineraries.title: Segovia day trip from Madrid
itineraries.creator: willflyforfood
itineraries.summary: Roman aqueduct, the fairytale Alcázar and the cathedral, with roast suckling pig for lunch. About half an hour by high-speed train from Chamartín.

items.name: AVE from Chamartín to Segovia-Guiomar
items.note: About 30 minutes. The station is 8 km out: take bus 11 or 12 into town.

items.name: Mesón de Cándido
items.note: Lunch: cochinillo asado. Or Restaurante José María.
